slides.3.title: The Eight Alentejo Sub-Regions Explained
slides.3.html:
Alentejo DOC covers one third of southern Portugal and has eight sub-regions, each with different soils and microclimates.

Sub-region Location Soil Character
Portalegre Northernmost (500-800m) Granite Coolest, elegant whites, a rising star in recent years
Borba North-central Marble・limestone Major large-winery area (Borba cooperative), rounded reds
Redondo Central Granite・schist Higher altitude, cooler than average, refined style
Reguengos South-central Granite・clay Reguengos cooperative (the largest), Esporão winery
Évora Central (provincial capital) Varied Capital of Alentejo, UNESCO World Heritage city
Vidigueira South Schist・limestone Most famous for whites (Antão Vaz), Soares da Silva
Granja-Amareleja Far south-east Sandstone・limestone Hottest and driest, close to Spain, sun-baked fortified-style wines
Moura Southernmost Schist・sand Closest to the Algarve, tropical fruit style
slides.4.title: Alentejo's Winery Revolution: The Rise After the 1990s
slides.4.html:
Before the 1990s, Alentejo's wines were made mainly by cooperatives and quality was rough. After the 1990s, a revolution began.

🔑 Three key factors behind the rise

  1. Private winery investment: large sums were invested, bringing in stainless steel fermentation tanks, French oak barrels and modern winemaking equipment
  2. Temperature control: high summer heat had been the biggest obstacle; temperature-controlled fermentation keeps white wines fresh
  3. Rediscovery of Alicante Bouschet: this French teinturier variety showed unexpectedly high quality in Alentejo

🏆 Leading producers

  • Esporão: in the Reguengos sub-region, Portugal's largest exporting winery and a pioneer of organic farming
  • Herdade do Mouchão: classic style, the benchmark for Alicante Bouschet, needing 10+ years of ageing
  • Cartuxa (Fundação Eugénio de Almeida): a historic brand of Évora; its flagship Pera Manca is Alentejo's most legendary wine
  • Cortes de Cima: a winery founded by Danish immigrants, a Syrah pioneer, close to Vidigueira
slides.5.question: Which Alentejo sub-region is known for the highest altitude (500-800m) and the coolest climate, and has recently become a rising star for quality white wines?
slides.5.explanation: Portalegre is Alentejo's northernmost and highest (500-800m) sub-region, with a cooler climate than the others. Its granite soils and lower temperatures help whites keep more fresh acidity and minerality, and in recent years it has become a rising star for Alentejo's quality whites.
slides.6.question: Which winery produces Alentejo's best-known flagship wine, "Pera Manca", regarded as Alentejo's most legendary flagship?
slides.6.explanation: Pera Manca is produced by Cartuxa (Fundação Eugénio de Almeida) in Évora and is Alentejo's most legendary flagship wine. It is released only in the best vintages, in both red and white versions.
